messages:
incident-bot: [Pager] HIGH severity: customer=Opal Orbit (enterprise-opal) - sudden 429 rate spike observed from vpc-dedicated-pool-12, error rate 17% over 5m, affecting realtime inference routes. Link: https://telemetry.redwood.internal/incidents/2039991234

sara: I have the page. pulling traces and token-level metrics now. assigning to @mike_oncall for immediate mitigation.

mike_oncall: oncall ack. looking at the pool dashboard — tail latency OK but quota throttle counters climbing. seeing a burst from tenant(opal-ent-42) at ~13:10 UTC.

ashley_se: tagging in. this is the enterprise VPC tenant using reserved dedicated capacity. they have a contract clause for emergency adjustments; need SOC approval if we change quotas.

beth_support: customer on the line, they report user-facing 429s in production UI. they say traffic pattern is consistent with batch retry storm from internal pipeline. requesting temporary lift.

mike_oncall: quick triage: KV cache hit rates unchanged, no model OOMs, errors are returning 429s from rate-limiter service. suspect per-tenant token/sec enforcement triggered. pulling limiter logs: `tenant=opal-ent-42 rate=4200 tok/s limit=1000 duration=00:04:12`

ashley_se: can we confirm this is not a malicious spike? customer claims legitimate backlog replay. any signature of token replay or identical request hashes?

mike_oncall: sampling request ids -> many unique request_ids, consistent user agent header `opal-batch/1.2`. looks like legitimate.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook match: `enterprise-rate-lift` (priority: manual approval required). Steps: 1) Confirm customer ownership and contract, 2) Apply temporary per-tenant rate override on vpc-dedicated-pool-12, 3) Monitor error rate and CPU/GPU utilization, 4) Rollback after 30m or when spike subsides. Link: https://runbooks.internal/enterprise-rate-lift

ashley_se: I have SOC on standby. Beth, can you confirm the customer contract has emergency lift clause?

beth_support: Confirmed. Contract ID OPAL-ENTERPRISE-2024 clause 4.2 permits 1 emergency lift per quarter with approval. customer signed.

sara: Security checks: auth logs show requests signed with the tenant's key, no IMS anomalies. good to proceed.

mike_oncall: Preparing temporary override. Will target `tenant=opal-ent-42` on pool `vpc-dedicated-pool-12` with a 4x multiplier for 20 minutes and a hard cap to avoid noisy neighbor issues. Command: ```sh
# apply override
redwoodctl quota override --tenant opal-ent-42 --pool vpc-dedicated-pool-12 --multiplier 4 --duration 20m --tag incident-2039991234
```

rdw-eng-lead: +1 to proceed, but set alert if CPU or GPU utilization > 85% or latency p50 > 200ms. Also create fallback policy to reroute to cheaper region if pool saturates.

mike_oncall: executing now.```sh
redwoodctl quota override --tenant opal-ent-42 --pool vpc-dedicated-pool-12 --multiplier 4 --duration 20m --tag incident-2039991234 && echo "override-applied"
```

incident-bot: Action logged: `quota_override` by mike_oncall at 2039991270 (audit id: 9f3a2c).

mike_oncall: override-applied. monitoring...

sara: metrics update: error rate dropping from 17% -> 2% in 45s, requests passing through. latency stable. GPU util +6%. no spillover to other tenants so far.

beth_support: customer confirms reduced 429s on their side. they still see some backlog processing but UX recovered. :thumbsup:

ashley_se: SOC please sign post for audit trail. we have approval in chat and command audit. I will file emergency lift incident in compliance tracker.

ops-runbook-bot: Reminder: auto-rollback scheduled at +20m (2039992399). Set monitoring alerts for early rollback if adverse metrics.

mike_oncall: setting a mid-check at +10m to reassess. Also creating temporary rate-limit rule: `deny-if-total-cpu>85%` to auto-throttle the override.

rdw-eng-lead: Good. Also add a note for postmortem: we need to evaluate why customer's batch retried; recommend a cached-queue pattern or staged retries.

sara: mid-check 10m: error rate steady ~1.1%, latency normal. no signs of cascade.

beth_support: Customer requests confirmation when we rollback so they can throttle their pipeline. They want a 5m heads-up.

mike_oncall: we'll provide 5m heads-up. scheduling a manual rollback at ~2039992360 if no regression.

incident-bot: Scheduled reminder: `rollback-check` at 2039992310 (in 10m).

sara: prepping short note for the customer: "We applied a temporary emergency override to your dedicated pool; this will be rolled back in ~20m. Please begin throttling retries now to avoid recurrence."

beth_support: sent to customer. they acknowledged and will start throttling.

mike_oncall: performing pre-rollback checks now: CPU/GPU util within limits, error rates <1.5%, queue drain progressing. All good.

mike_oncall: rolling back override in 30s.```sh
redwoodctl quota rollback --audit-tag incident-2039991234
```

incident-bot: Action logged: `quota_rollback` by mike_oncall at 2039991365 (audit id: b7e8d3).

sara: post-rollback metrics: 429s did not resurface, error rate at 0.8%. customer confirms no visible problem.

ashley_se: closing emergency lift request in compliance tracker and adding the approval screenshot.

rdw-eng-lead: Good work. Please create a short incident summary for postmortem: include timeline, reason (customer replay), mitigation (temp override), and recommended follow-ups (customer retry-backoff, alert thresholds, add auto-runbook for enterprise lifts).

beth_support: I'll own the customer follow-up and scheduling a technical sync with Opal Orbit to implement safer retry patterns tomorrow.

sara: assigning postmortem doc to `ENG-OPS-2039991234` and linking runbook.

mike_oncall: handing off to day shift. oncall clear.

rdw-eng-lead: thanks team. I'll mark incident as resolved once the postmortem is uploaded.

incident-bot: Incident state: RESOLVED at 2039991399. Duration: ~165s.
